instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The cruciate injury sustained in 1996/97 and Dalglish's more conservative side left him a rotation defender rather than the composed ball-player of the Keegan years.
Arrived in February and went straight into the side; an Argentina starter and already one of the best pure screening midfielders anywhere.
An ankle problem cost him much of the season, but at twenty-nine he was still an elite all-round midfielder and Germany’s captain.
A British-record fee for a goalkeeper and, on ability, a fair one: outstanding reflexes and a genuine Scotland number one, in a Sunderland side that gave him a great deal to do.
Seventeen and thrown into a relegated QPR side; rated as the raw teenager.
Thirteen starts and six goals after a 7m move before injury took the season; the form itself was good.
African Footballer of the Year two seasons earlier; a genuinely creative number ten in a mid-table Coventry side.
The Euro 2004 golden boot season carried into a genuinely sharper year: elite acceleration and a much improved first touch, still a narrow all-round game.
A first season spent being told he was too slight for England; the ball retention under pressure was already the best at the club.
Moved into the centre and ran Tottenham’s season from there; an elite central midfielder by the end of it, which is what the bid the following summer was for.
The one season the finishing caught up with the running: twelve goals before a January move to Manchester City.
The season that made him: the driving force of a Wigan side that finished tenth, and an England-squad conversation by the end of it.
Four games into his Fulham career he ruptured a knee ligament and lost fifteen months. Rated as the player he was in those four games, not on the minutes.
His most productive season and the closest he came to sustaining it: seven goals from the left in a side that survived on the last day.
His first full season and an immediate jump: left-sided, quick and much the most comfortable passer in the Liverpool back four.
Two goals and six assists, and for half a season Arsenal’s best player: an outstanding carrier of the ball in tight spaces. Output is the poorest possible guide to him.
Three years on from the Arsenal peak, by way of a failed move to Barcelona: a peripheral loan player whose sharpness had gone.
Signed in January on the strength of an outstanding left foot and a genuine passing range; slow, and the fitness was already a question at 22.
